title: Chain commands: run the next one only on success or on failure
summary: Shows how to join commands on one line. You can continue only when the previous command worked, run a fallback when it failed, run commands one after another no matter what, and group several commands together.

aliases.text: run second command only if first succeeds
run command if previous one failed
group commands in bash with parentheses
semicolon versus double ampersand in shell
выполнить команду только если предыдущая успешна

steps.explain: Continue only on success. The folder is created first; the 'ready' message appears only if that worked. If the command after 'and' fails, the 'or' part runs as a fallback.
steps.cmd: mkdir -p <DIR> && echo "folder ready" || echo "could not create <DIR>"

steps.explain: Run a fallback when a test fails. test -f checks that a file exists; with no such file, the 'or' part prints the message.
steps.expect: missing: notes.txt when that file does not exist in the folder.

steps.explain: Run commands one after another. A semicolon runs the next command even when the previous one failed, so the last line still prints.
steps.cmd: echo "step one"; false; echo "step two still runs after a failed step"
steps.expect: step one, then step two still runs after a failed step.

steps.explain: Group commands in parentheses, which run in a separate shell. The cd inside does not change the folder you are in; the second pwd shows your original folder.
steps.expect: The folder path first, then the original folder path.

placeholders.name: DIR
placeholders.description: Folder to visit inside the group

steps.explain: Group commands with braces, so one redirection applies to all of them. The braces need a semicolon before the closing brace.
steps.expect: No output on screen. The log file now holds the message and today's date.
